seoTitle: How to Fit Text in a Cell on Google Sheets
metaDescription: Stop text from spilling over or getting cut off in Google Sheets using text wrapping, cell clipping, and auto-fit column widths.
intro: Long text spilling over cells or getting awkwardly cut off is one of the most common formatting annoyances in Google Sheets. This guide covers three practical fixes — text wrapping, cell clipping, and auto-fitting column widths — so your spreadsheet tables stay clean and readable.

steps.heading: Understand the text overflow problem
steps.body: Long text in a narrow cell will either spill into neighboring cells or get visually cut off, depending on your formatting settings.

steps.heading: Use text wrapping
steps.body: Open the text wrapping tool options in the top formatting bar and choose the wrap setting to stack long sentences vertically within a cell.

steps.heading: Set up cell clipping
steps.body: Use the clip option to hide overflow text without deleting any of the underlying data.

steps.heading: Auto-fit column widths
steps.body: Double-click a column border to automatically resize it based on its content.

steps.heading: Adjust row heights
steps.body: Resize row heights to match wrapped text so nothing looks cramped.

steps.heading: Apply formatting in bulk
steps.body: Select multiple columns at once to apply consistent formatting across your whole sheet.

faq.question: What's the difference between wrapping and clipping text?
faq.answer: Wrapping stacks long text vertically within the same cell so it's all visible, while clipping hides the overflow without deleting the underlying data.

faq.question: How do I quickly resize a column to fit its content?
faq.answer: Double-clicking the border between two column headers will auto-fit the column width to its content.

faq.question: Will wrapping text change my row height automatically?
faq.answer: Row height often needs to be adjusted separately after wrapping to make sure the wrapped text displays cleanly.

faq.question: Can I apply the same formatting to multiple columns at once?
faq.answer: Yes, selecting several columns before applying wrap or clip settings lets you format them all in bulk for consistency.
